title: Students and community members protest school flag policy in Sonoma
seoTitle: Sonoma students protest school flag policy

tea.why: The school board voted to restrict the display of Pride flags on school grounds, leading to the removal of the Progress Pride flag.
tea.want: Protesters want the district to reverse its new flag policy and allow the continued display of the Progress Pride flag.
tea.changed: Oct 13: Hundreds of students and community members held a walkout and rally at Sonoma Valley High School to protest the policy change.

summary: On October 13, hundreds of students and community members gathered at Sonoma Valley High School to protest a new flag policy adopted by the Sonoma Valley Unified School District. The board voted 3-2 on October 8 to restrict the display of symbolic flags, requiring only American and California state flags to fly during the academic day. The policy resulted in the removal of the Progress Pride flag, which had been displayed at the high school since 2019. Organised by the school's Gender & Sexualities Alliance, participants held a walkout and rally, with further demonstrations planned, including the planting of flags on the school lawn. School board President David Bell defended the policy, stating the district aims to represent all students equally.
demands: Allow the display of the Progress Pride flag
response: School board President David Bell stated that the board's role is to represent all students equally and that the policy ensures the district does not favor specific viewpoints.

updates.text: The Sonoma Valley Unified School District Board of Trustees voted 3-2 to approve a new policy restricting symbolic flags on school grounds.
Hundreds of students and community members held a walkout and rally at Sonoma Valley High School to protest the policy.
